architecture.title: Two agents, one local model — OpenClaw and Hermes on the Spark host, no sandbox
architecture.caption: vLLM serves the agent-ready model on the Spark's :8000. OpenClaw (config in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) and Hermes (config in ~/.hermes, set with `hermes config set`) both call it through the OpenAI-compatible /v1 API and run the returned tool calls themselves, directly on the host. You reach OpenClaw's dashboard through an SSH tunnel and Hermes' TUI through SSH. Messaging gateways are optional; the playbooks say restrict them to your own user ID and never expose the dashboard or :8000 publicly.

sequence.title: One tool call, end to end — the model proposes, the agent executes
sequence.caption: Both agents work the same way at the API level: they send the conversation plus tool definitions, the model answers with a tool_call (name + JSON arguments), the agent runs the tool on the host and sends the result back as a `tool` message, and the model writes the final answer. Lab 17-2 tests exactly these four steps (P1–P4) plus restraint (P5). There is no sandbox here: the tool runs as your user.

steps.label: run it (as your user, no sandbox)
